newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson Breweries cuts beer price in Ontario.
newsitem.headline: Molson Breweries cuts beer price in Ontario.

text.p: Molson Breweries said on Wednesday that it will cut its price for beer in Canada's most populous province of Ontario by C$3.00 a case to C$26.15 for a case of 24 beers for two weeks starting June 30.

Molson said the cuts will include the following brands: Brador, Molson Canadian, Molson Canadian Ice, Molson Canadian Light, Coors, Coors Light, Molson Export, Foster's, Molson Golden, Miller Genuine Draft, Miller Genuine Draft Light, Miller Lite, Miller High Life, Molson Ultra, Old Vienna, Molson Dry, Pilsner and Molson Stock Ale.
Molson Breweries is owned 40 percent each by Molson Cos Ltd and Foster's Brewing Group Ltd of Australia, while Philip Morris Cos Inc subsidiary Miller Brewing Co owns 20 percent.
Molson Breweries said it sells over 24 million bottles of beer in a two-week period and said it hopes the price discount will be passed on by bars, restaurants and other licensed beer sales.
Molson Breweries said earlier this year that it holds about 52.2 percent of the market share in Ontario, while its biggest competitor John Labatt Ltd holds 40.5 percent.
